question: Webhook URL placement: env var only, file only, or both?
answer: Both, with env winning. Resolution order: (1) `JARVIS_DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL` env, (2) `~/.jarvis/discord.json` with key `webhook_url`, (3) None → silent. Env wins because dispatch under env override (e.g. `JARVIS_DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL=<url2> python -m jarvis_orchestrate ...`) is the obvious 'route this run elsewhere' workflow. File-only would force operators to edit a file every time they want to A/B routes; env-only would force them to re-export every shell session. Both, with env precedence, is the cheapest reading of `~/.jarvis/quota_caps.json` + `JARVIS_QUOTA_CAPS_PATH` precedent already shipped in plan 2026-04-30-001 F004.
rationale: Operator override should be one keystroke; persistent default should be set-and-forget. Mirroring quota-caps precedent means operators don't learn two patterns.

question: Rate limiting / debounce: implement first-pass or defer?
answer: Defer. D059 is silent on rate limiting. The estimated traffic ('~8-15 Discord posts/day for typical 1-2 active plan workload') is below any reasonable rate-limit threshold; Discord's documented webhook rate limit is 30 requests / 60s / channel which is ~3000× our expected rate. Implementing rate-limiting prophylactically without observed traffic problems builds wrong abstractions. Re-evaluate when (a) operator runs >5 plans concurrently, OR (b) a flaky network triggers retry storms (which the current 'no retry, fail-soft' design already prevents), OR (c) Discord 429s are observed in stderr warn-once. Until then, no rate-limiter, no debounce queue, no request batching. Recorded explicitly here so a future reviewer doesn't reintroduce rate-limiting silently.
rationale: Compact-first; reread the brief: 'Rate limiting and mentions can be explicit deferred decisions unless D059 already requires them.' D059 does not. The smallest workable sink defers everything not in the operator pain path.

question: @mention behavior in v1: where does the user-ID source come from, and what does v1 actually do?
answer: v1 generates NO @mention content AND sets `allowed_mentions.parse = []` ALWAYS. Operator review surfaced that the original D003 referenced `<@USER_ID>` body markers without specifying where the USER_ID comes from — leaving the mention contract underspecified. v1 closes that ambiguity by removing mentions entirely: emit-site bodies are plain prose with no `<@USER_ID>` / `@here` / `@everyone` markers; the Discord payload's `allowed_mentions.parse` field is hardcoded to `[]` so even an operator-edited body containing such markers cannot accidentally ping. D059's escalation @mention requirement is acknowledged but deferred to v2 with a concrete config shape: `~/.jarvis/discord.json` gains a `mention_user_ids: list[str]` array (e.g. `['305274112323584000']`); when severity=='escalation' AND mention_user_ids is non-empty, v2 will (a) prepend the IDs as `<@id> ` prefix to the rendered body, AND (b) set `allowed_mentions.parse = []` while populating `allowed_mentions.users = mention_user_ids` — this is Discord's documented per-id whitelist, safer than `parse: ['users']` which would parse ALL `<@id>` markers in the body. v2 is a follow-up plan; v1 ships mention-free.
rationale: Operator review: 'either no mention content is generated in v1, only allowed_mentions is controlled, or add mention_user_ids in ~/.jarvis/discord.json. Don't leave this implicit.' v1 takes the strictest read (no content, empty parse) so the contract is unambiguous. Documenting the v2 shape in this decision means a future implementer doesn't relitigate the user-ID source.

question: Event envelope shape: how compact?
answer: Seven fields, frozen: kind (str — extensible vocabulary, not a closed enum, so adding a new event kind in a future plan is a one-line emit-site change), severity (str — closed vocabulary 'info' | 'action_required' | 'escalation'), plan_id (str), feature_id (str | None), body (str — markdown, sink-renders-directly), action_link (str | None — required when severity=='escalation'), timestamp (datetime). NO sink-specific fields. NO embed structure. NO color codes. NO icon URLs. NO retry metadata. NO routing tags. Sinks render `body` directly; Discord may also pass `body` as `content` and use `username='Jarvis'` as the only consistent decoration. The compact shape is the contract. Adding fields requires a follow-up decision record because every additional field forces every sink to handle it. Both notify.py (terminal-notifier title/subtitle/group) and notify_discord.py (content + username) project from the envelope; their projection logic is the per-sink responsibility.
rationale: The brief said 'Define a compact internal event envelope' and 'F002 taxonomy small'. Seven fields is the smallest set that preserves enough context to render a useful notification AND to gate on level + severity. Anything below that hides routing info; anything above that bakes channel-specific concerns into the shared contract.

question: Sanitization discipline: how do we keep webhook URLs out of committed code?
answer: Three guard rails compounding: (1) `~/.jarvis/discord.json` lives outside the repo tree (operator-managed, like `~/.jarvis/quota_caps.json` and `~/.jarvis/quota_calibration.json`); (2) `JARVIS_DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL` env is operator-set, never committed; (3) test fixtures use `https://example.invalid/webhook` as the placeholder URL — `.invalid` is RFC 2606 reserved, will never resolve to a real Discord endpoint. F022's existing `scripts/sanitization_check.py` already scans for committed secrets and runs in CI; F001 + F004 acceptance criteria explicitly require zero hits from that scanner against the new files. No webhook-URL-shaped string (matching `discord.com/api/webhooks/...`) may appear anywhere in the repo. If F022's scanner does not currently pattern-match Discord webhook URLs, F004 includes adding that pattern as a regression guard.
rationale: Plan B introduces a new secret class. Without explicit discipline, operator workstation copy-paste accidents leak the URL into git. The .invalid TLD trick is industry standard for placeholder URLs in tests.

question: Why F003 'wire emit points' is one slice, not five (one per emit point)?
answer: Because the emit sites are intra-supervisor surgical edits with shared structural concerns (build NotifyEvent, ensure INBOX write precedes dispatch_event call, ensure escalation events carry action_link). Splitting into five per-emit-point features would cause five auditor passes against essentially the same shared invariant ('INBOX-first, then dispatch, action_link required on escalation'). One feature lets the auditor verify the invariant once across all sites. The acceptance criteria itemize all 5 sites so coverage is explicit.
rationale: Locked-AC + slice-sizing memory says split when concerns differ; merge when concerns are shared. This is the latter.

question: Why no slash-command / inbound Discord integration in this plan?
answer: Bidirectional integration (Discord → supervisor, e.g. operator typing `/jarvis approve <plan-id>` in the channel) requires a stateful HTTP listener, a shared secret rotation story, identity verification (which operator is invoking), and operator-account binding to plan permissions. None of those are present in the unidirectional sink. Adding bidirectional in this plan would 5-10× the surface area and 5× the security review. Outbound-only is the smallest workable observability sink. Inbound is a separate plan if/when operators ask for it after the outbound sink lands and gets used.
rationale: D059 + the brief both scope this as 'notification sink', not 'control plane'. Keeping the surface unidirectional is what makes the plan landable in a few hours rather than days.

question: Terminal-sink (notify.py) adapter compatibility — does it stay on its keyword-arg signature or migrate to NotifyEvent?
answer: Both. notify.py keeps its existing public `notify(title, message, *, subtitle=None, group='jarvis')` keyword-arg signature as the rendering primitive (no breaking change for any external caller), AND gains a sibling `notify_event(event: NotifyEvent) -> bool` shim that projects NotifyEvent → keyword args: title=`Jarvis [{plan_id}]`, subtitle=`{kind}` (e.g. 'breaker_tripped'), message=`body[:140]` (truncated to fit notification UX), group=`plan_id` (per-plan stack groupable for clear-all). dispatch_event in notify_event.py calls notify_event (the shim), NOT notify directly. Existing supervisor call sites that today invoke `notify.notify(title=..., message=..., subtitle=..., group=...)` migrate to dispatch_event(NotifyEvent(...)) in F003. Acceptance gates this with a regression test (F004 acceptance #8): for a fixed set of 3 fixture events (one per severity level), the projected title/subtitle/message/group must equal a documented before/after table, so any future change to the projection rule is caught explicitly.
rationale: Operator review: 'notify.py does not currently consume NotifyEvent. F002 says both sinks consume the same envelope. That means adapting terminal notifier call sites, not just adding Discord. Acceptance should explicitly require terminal notifications still render equivalent title/message/subtitle after the adapter.' This decision pins the projection rule and the regression test that defends it.

question: PLAN_BOUNDARY_KINDS — where lives the definition of which kinds count as plan-boundary?
answer: Module constant in notify_event.py. `PLAN_BOUNDARY_KINDS = frozenset({'volley_start', 'volley_terminal', 'signoff'})`. Closed set, asserted in tests. Future kinds (e.g. 'plan_locked', 'plan_completed') added by explicit edit to this constant + a paired decision record explaining why the new kind crosses the plan-boundary threshold. The level matrix predicate references this constant directly so 'normal' admits any event whose kind is in PLAN_BOUNDARY_KINDS regardless of severity. This avoids the original ambiguity where 'normal' was prose-defined as 'plan-boundary kinds' without naming them, leaving gate_cleared and future kinds ambiguously routed.
rationale: Operator review: 'normal says action_required/escalation plus plan-boundary kinds. Good, but define plan-boundary exactly: volley_start, volley_terminal, signoff. Otherwise gate_cleared and future kinds will be interpreted inconsistently.' Encoding the set as a code-level constant + tests asserting its exact contents prevents drift.

question: Sanitizer pattern for Discord webhook URLs — conditional or hard requirement?
answer: Hard requirement, F004 acceptance items 9-10. The Discord webhook URL pattern `https?://discord(?:app)?\.com/api/webhooks/\d+/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+` MUST be a recognized signature in `scripts/sanitization_check.py` by the time F004 lands. If the existing scanner does not match this pattern, F004 implementation adds it (NOT a deferred prose item). A paired regression test drops a fake webhook-URL-shaped string (using fake-but-realistic IDs like `123456789012345678/aBcDeFgHiJkL_-mNoPqRsTuVwXyZ123456`) into a tracked-not-ignored temp file and asserts sanitization_check.py exits non-zero, so future sanitizer rewrites cannot silently regress the pattern. The original D005 said 'if scanner doesn't pattern-match, add it' — that conditional left a way for the implementer to skip the work. D010 promotes it to mandatory.
rationale: Operator review: 'D005 says if scanner doesn't pattern-match Discord webhooks, add it. Make that an acceptance item, not conditional prose. This plan introduces a new secret class.' Webhook URLs are the secret this plan introduces; sanitizer coverage is the existing F022 mechanism that prevents leaks. Mandatory means we test the pattern's presence, not just its conditional addition.

title: Brand-aware env+config naming with legacy fallback
body: Original plan referenced JARVIS_DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL + ~/.jarvis/discord.json. Implementation honors BOTH the legacy and modern brand: env vars accept DONTPANIC_DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL (modern wins) OR JARVIS_DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL (legacy fallback); config files at $DONTPANIC_HOME/discord.json (modern) OR $JARVIS_HOME/discord.json (legacy). Mirrors the global_config.dontpanic_home() resolution pattern from plan 2026-05-03-001 and the brand-rename project memory. Operators with existing JARVIS_* config don’t need to migrate.

title: Plan close-out: F001-F004 all green, full sweep 1676 passed
body: All 4 features shipped and verified. Net +88 tests over prior baseline (86 new Discord tests + 2 absorbed in secret-shape snapshot bump from 8→9). Manual-direct discipline per established pattern. Followed the per-emit-site INBOX-first invariant: every dispatch_event call site verified to write the durable INBOX entry first, then fire live sinks (Discord + terminal). The transitional pattern of keeping existing notify.notify calls AND adding parallel dispatch_event with sinks=(SINK_DISCORD,) avoids the double-fire regression a full notify.notify→dispatch_event migration would have introduced. Future cleanup plan can drop notify.notify calls and use dispatch_event’s default sinks once operators confirm the uniform Jarvis-[{plan_id}] terminal title format is acceptable.
